issue:generate.description: Generate ticket descriptions from local files, repo-scoped artifacts via --repos, URLs, ticket keys, or tracker browse URLs. Tracker browse URLs (e.g. https://<org>.atlassian.net/browse/<KEY>) are automatically detected and fetched via the tracker REST API instead of scraping HTML; self-hosted instances are supported when atlassian.baseUrl is configured. Local .md, .json, .yaml, and .yml files that parse as tickets are imported as tickets; files that are not recognized as ticket-formatted content remain plain file sources. When --repos points to a local checkout, wf bootstraps config from that repo and accepts either module.exports or export default in wf.config.js, including ESM repos. Repo-scoped generation now inspects both prior ticket descriptions and prior plan artifacts so recurrence analysis and synthesis prompts can reuse earlier implementation context. AI synthesis always runs on every source to enrich and standardise the output. Generated output enforces formal writing conventions (concise prose, no contractions, active voice, British English) before display or save. Blank AI generate-stage responses fail fast with provider-aware diagnostics. Can use an agent backend when stages.generate.backend is set to agent

issue:implement.description: Carry out an implementation plan from a ticket-backed, hashed, or custom plan artifact. Delegates the generate-and-verify loop to the configured backend (Anthropic Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK, or Claude CLI headless mode) based on stages.implement.provider and stages.implement.backend. Progress events are streamed to the terminal so you can follow task and tool activity while edits are being generated. All backends emit stable task and tool progress lines plus explicit file mutation logs and verification logs so terminal output stays human-readable while the agent works. Verification commands are expected to be repo-root-relative; stale plan artifacts that still embed redundant repo-selection `cd` prefixes are normalized, while cross-repo directory jumps are treated as setup errors. Set stages.implement.provider and stages.implement.backend in wf.config to select the backend. Use backend: agent with provider anthropic or openai for the Agent SDK path, or backend: cli with provider anthropic or openai for the CLI headless mode (Claude CLI or Codex CLI respectively). The Anthropic backend explicitly loads ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and the repository-root CLAUDE.md, warning when either file is missing. The OpenAI backend loads ~/.openai/OPENAI.md and the repository-root .openai/OPENAI.md with the same warning behavior and only exposes an exact-match verify_command tool for whitelisted verification commands. When running from source, use `yarn start issue:implement ...` for the implementation stage and `yarn start issue:commit -c` to stage the final conventional commit once the work is accepted. Unsupported providers (google, deepseek) fail fast with a clear error listing supported providers. backend: standard is rejected at runtime because the implement stage requires an agent-capable backend. Blank AI findings responses fail fast with provider-aware diagnostics instead of generic parse errors. Run issue:fetch then issue:plan before calling this command for ticket-backed workflows. When a hashed plan artifact is provided, the action is inferred from the filename/manifest and `--action` becomes optional, but any supplied action is still validated against the resolved artifact. Before implementation, the command runs an interactive branch creation workflow: checks the working tree for uncommitted changes (stashing if needed), detects and pulls the source branch (dev or main), then prompts for branch name confirmation. Use --silent to auto-stash without prompting; branch selection and naming still prompt when a TTY is available. Use --no-branch to skip branch creation and work directly on the source branch. Use --branch-name-pattern to override the branch name validation regex from git.branchNamePattern config. Examples: wf issue:implement PROJ-123 | wf issue:implement 2026-05-04-1a2b3c4d-fix-plan.json | wf issue:implement PROJ-123 --repos my-repo | wf issue:implement PROJ-123 --silent | wf issue:implement PROJ-123 --no-branch | wf issue:implement PROJ-123 --dry-run

issue:plan.description: Plan ticket implementation from a local artifact or repo-scoped custom artifact. If a local artifact is not found, the command will attempt to fetch it from the primary tracker. Use --force to fetch and recreate artifacts. Repo-scoped planning inspects both prior ticket descriptions and prior plan artifacts so recurrence analysis and planning prompts can reuse earlier implementation context. Planning prompts include detected repository test conventions and ecosystem-specific verification guidance so generated steps match local test patterns and only reference allowed command forms. Targeted verification commands are interpreted as repo-root-relative: redundant `cd <repo>` prefixes are normalized away, while commands that change directories outside the selected repository are rejected.
